==English== ===Etymology=== {{ety|en|:inh|enm:intelligence|tree=1}} From {{inh|en|enm|intelligence}}, from {{der|en|fro|intelligence}}, from {{der|en|la|intelligentia}}, which is most likely from {{af|la|inter-|legere|nocat=1}}. {{dbt|en|intelligentsia}}. ===Pronunciation=== * {{IPA|en|/ɪnˈtɛl.ɪ.d͡ʒəns/}} * {{audio|en|En-us-intelligence.ogg|a=US}} * {{hyph|en|in|tel|li|gence}} ===Noun=== {{en-noun|~}} # {{lb|en|mostly|uncountable}} The [[capacity]] of [[mind]], especially to [[understand]] [[principle]]s, [[truth]]s, [[fact]]s or [[meaning]]s, [[acquire]] [[knowledge]], and [[apply]] it to [[practice]]; the [[ability]] to [[comprehend]] and [[learn]]; the ability to process sentient experience to generate true beliefs with a justified degree of confidence. #: {{syn|en|brightness|intellect|smartness|wit|Thesaurus:intelligence}} #: {{ant|en|unintelligence}} #* {{RQ:Burroughs Tarzan of the Apes|5|passage=Not so, however, with Tarzan, the man-child. His life amidst the dangers of the jungle had taught him to meet emergencies with self-confidence, and his higher '''intelligence''' resulted in a quickness of mental action far beyond the powers of the apes.}} #* '''1936 Feb.''', {{w|F. Scott Fitzgerald}}, "{{w|The Crack-Up}}", ''{{w|Esquire (magazine)|Esquire}}'': ...the test of a first-rate '''intelligence''' is the ability to hold two opposed ideas in the mind at the same time, and still retain the ability to function. ## {{lb|en|psychology}} An individual's [[expected]] relative [[performance]] in a [[cognitive test]]. ##: {{coi|en|[[intelligence quotient|'''intelligence''' quotient]]}} ##* {{quote-journal|en|date=2013-07-19||Ian Sample|volume=189|issue=6|page=34|Irregular bedtimes may affect children's brains|w:The Guardian Weekly|text=Irregular bedtimes may disrupt healthy brain development in young children, according to a study of '''intelligence''' and sleeping habits.{{pb}}Going to bed at a different time each night affected girls more than boys, but both fared worse on mental tasks than children who had a set bedtime, researchers found.|articleurl=https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2013/jul/08/irregular-bedtimes-affect-childrens-brains|archiveurl=https://web.archive.org/web/20261018015540/https://www.theguardian.com/lifeandstyle/2013/jul/08/irregular-bedtimes-affect-childrens-brains|archivedate=18 October 2026}} ## {{lb|en|mostly|uncountable}} The [[quality]] of making use or having made use of such capacities: [[depth]] of [[understanding]], [[mental]] [[quickness]]. # {{lb|en|countable}} An [[entity]] that has such capacities. #: {{syn|en|Thesaurus:sentient}} #* {{RQ:Tennyson In Memoriam|LXXXIII|118|The great '''Intelligences''' fair
     That range above our mortal state,
     In circle round the blessed gate,
Received and gave him welcome there.}} #* {{quote-book|en|1936|Rollo Ahmed|The Black Art|publisher=w:John Long Ltd|location=w:London||275|But there are latent powers within man alone that are not yet fully understood and{{…}} we cannot definitely state what is, and what is not, due to the interference or influence of discarnate '''intelligences'''.}} # {{lb|en|mostly|uncountable}} {{1|information}}, often [[secret]], about an [[enemy]] or about [[hostile]] [[activity|activities]]. #* {{quote-book|en|year=1909|title=The Lives of the Twelve Caesers|author=C. Suetonius Tranquillus|translator=Alexander Thomson|editor=T. Forester|location=London|publisher=George Bell & Sons|page=75|pageurl=https://archive.org/details/livesoftwelvecae0000suet_o9f1/page/75/mode/1up |text=After the subjugation of Spain, while Cæsar was meditating an expedition against the Dacians and Parthians, he was sent before him to Apollonia, where he applied himself to his studies; until receiving '''intelligence''' that his uncle was murdered, and that he was appointed his heir, he hesitated for some time whether he should call to his aid the legions stationed in the neighbourhood; {{...|but he abandoned the design as rash and premature}} .}} ## {{lb|en|countable}} A [[political]] or [[military]] [[department]], [[agency]] or [[unit]] designed to [[gather]] [[information]], usually [[secret]], about the [[enemy]] or about [[hostile]] [[activity|activities]]. # {{lb|en|dated}} {{1|acquaintance}}; [[intercourse]]; [[familiarity]]. #* {{quote-book|en|1650|w:Thomas Fuller|A Pisgah-Sight of Palestine and the Confines Thereof|https://www.google.com/books/edition/h/PdBVtYvJwPIC|location=w:London|106|Yet ''Josephus'' tells us of ''Phiala'', a ſpring{{…}} into which ''Philip'' the Tetrarch caſt chaffe to try the experiment, and it was rendred up again into the ſtreame of ''Iordan''. Whence he concluded, that this river entertained an underground ''intelligence'' with that fountain.}} #* {{RQ:Clarendon History|I|48|He liv’d rather in a fair '''Intelligence''' than any Friendſhip
